ops.title: Build/venv quirks in cc-transcript — broken asdf cargo shim breaks uv sync; use uv run --no-sync; jj-colocated repo

ops.body:
In /Users/yasyf/Code/cc-transcript (maturin build with a Rust extension):

- `uv sync` triggers a maturin rebuild that fails because the asdf cargo shim (`~/.asdf/shims/cargo`, asdf 0.8.1 homebrew breakage) is broken. Workaround: `PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" uv sync ...`.
- Prefer `uv run --no-sync ...` for everything else — it avoids the rebuild entirely and is safe while parallel agents share the venv.
- **`uv sync` does NOT recompile the Rust ext after `rust/*`-only edits** — with no version bump it reports "Checked N packages" and the venv keeps the stale `_parser_rs` (so `@requires_rust` parity tests and new `#[pyfunction]`s silently won't appear). **`uv sync --reinstall-package cc-transcript` is NOT a reliable force-rebuild either** — uv can reinstall from a STALE cached wheel keyed by the (unchanged) `13.0.0` version, so the native code stays stale even after `--reinstall-package` (verified 2026-07-13: after `uv sync --reinstall-package cc-transcript` in a worktree, `dir(_parser_rs)` still lacked the newly-added symbols; bit both the ids lane and main during the v14 rewrite, failing dozens of `test_*_parity` tests with `AttributeError`). **Reliable forced rebuild:** `uv run --with maturin maturin develop --uv` (fetches maturin ephemerally — the venv doesn't ship it — and ALWAYS recompiles) or `uv sync --refresh-package cc-transcript` (invalidates the build cache). **Always verify freshness** before trusting a pytest gate: `uv run --no-sync python -c "from cc_transcript import _parser_rs; print(dir(_parser_rs))"` and confirm the new symbol is present. **And**: any `uv sync --extra dev --reinstall-package …` PRUNES the other extras from the shared venv (judge/sentiment vanish → test_similar/test_verdicts fail, lexicon spaCy tests skip) — always re-list every extra in the same command: `uv sync --extra dev --extra judge --extra sentiment --reinstall-package cc-transcript`.
- **Fresh worktree bootstrap: `uv sync` can fail at the editable maturin build and install ZERO deps.** In a pristine per-worktree venv, `uv sync --extra …` builds the editable `cc-transcript` wheel (a maturin compile) as part of the sync; if that compile fails (wrong/shared target dir, transient), the whole sync aborts and NONE of the runtime deps land — `anyio` etc. are missing and even pure-Python scripts (`scripts/gen_*_golden.py`) die with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'anyio'` (verified 2026-07-14, p2-context lane). **Fix: two-step** — `env -u VIRTUAL_ENV PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" uv sync --no-install-project --extra dev --extra judge --extra llm` (installs all deps, skips building the project) then `CARGO_TARGET_DIR="$PWD/.cargo-target" maturin develop --uv --release` (builds+installs the ext into the venv). Also unset `VIRTUAL_ENV` (`env -u VIRTUAL_ENV`) — the outer shell often points it at the MAIN worktree's `.venv`, and uv warns + can target the wrong env.
- **Shared cargo target collides across git worktrees** — the fleet points every worktree at one shared target (`~/.cargo/shared-target`). `cc-transcript-core` has the same package name+version (`0.9.0`) in every worktree, so a sibling lane building core (e.g. one branched before your commit) clobbers the shared `cc-transcript-core` dev-profile artifact, and your `maturin develop` / `cargo build -p cc-transcript-py` then links a STALE core — the py crate errors with `unresolved import cc_transcript_core::cost`, `parse_usage_value is private`, etc. even though your source is correct and `cargo metadata` resolves the py crate to YOUR worktree core (verified 2026-07-14: bit the p2 smallmods lane; `cargo build -p cc-transcript-core` recompiled the right source, yet the immediately-following py build still linked stale because a sibling re-clobbered between the two). **Fix: build the extension with a per-worktree `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`** (`CARGO_TARGET_DIR="$PWD/.cargo-target" uvx maturin develop`) — isolates from sibling clobbering (slow first compile, ~1-2 min; incremental after). Use the same isolated target for your `cargo test --workspace` / `--no-default-features` gates so they're race-free too. `cargo test` (test profile) is less contended than the dev+default slot maturin needs, so it may pass on the shared target while maturin fails.
- **AGENTS.md is rendered from `.claude/fragments/AGENTS.md/` by cc-guides** — editing AGENTS.md directly gets clobbered on the next `cc-guides render`; edit the fragment, run `cc-guides render` (bumps `.claude/fragments/cc-guides.lock`), and commit both. A PreToolUse hook surfaces this on direct edits.
- The repo is **jj-colocated** (`.jj/` exists); `git status` shows misleading index states. Commit via `jj split <paths> -m ...` / `jj commit -m ...`; history style is plain conventional commits, no emoji.
- Docs builds: sync docs+dev together — `PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" uv sync --extra dev --group docs` — then `uv run --no-sync great-docs build` (~3–6 min). **Beware:** a bare `uv sync --group docs` re-resolves the venv and DROPS the `dev` extra, so `pytest`/`ty` vanish (`No module named pytest` / `Failed to spawn: pytest`); passing agents that only sync docs will silently break the test env for everyone sharing the venv. great-docs sometimes logs "Dynamic introspection failed, retrying static" (also a benign "Cyclic aliases detected: cc_transcript.TranscriptEvent") — benign; verify by diffing generated `great-docs/reference/*.qmd` stems against the `reference:` contents in great-docs.yml.
- **`great-docs.yml` hard-codes a curated `reference:` list of public-API symbol names.** Renaming/removing an exported symbol (class or function) WITHOUT updating great-docs.yml fails the build with `ERROR: Configured reference item(s) not found in cc_transcript`. So any public-API rename surface includes great-docs.yml — and the `great-docs build` gate is what catches a missed entry (source/markdown greps won't, since it's a YAML config). The build must run against a freshly rebuilt extension (see the maturin/`--reinstall-package` note above) or it reports the OLD symbols as missing.

- This machine's global uv config sets an `exclude-newer` cutoff, so `uvx`/`uv pip install` silently ignore freshly published PyPI releases (uvx falls back to the prior version with a misleading error). To verify a new release locally: `uvx --exclude-newer-package "<pkg>=<tomorrow>Z" <pkg>==<ver> ...`. Other machines are unaffected.

**Why:** these failures look like project bugs but are environment quirks; without this, agents burn time re-diagnosing the cargo shim, racing the venv, or misreading a healthy release as broken.
**How to apply:** pass the PATH fix + --no-sync rules into any subagent/workflow prompt that touches this repo; never run bare `uv sync` in parallel fan-outs. See [[great-docs-executable-cells]] for docs-cell constraints.
